question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool scheduling mode in core, and should it require explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata before any early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level latency opportunity is real, but the implementation changes core runtime semantics and safety policy rather than repairing an already-defined behavior contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for early execution, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Block On Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat this as dependent on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract before scheduling can change.

options.title: Defer Runtime Semantics Change
options.body: Keep the current post-stream batching model if maintainers decide early execution is too risky or not worth the added runtime surface.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for early execution, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this person to both the agent-core loop and the AI/provider-stream extraction surfaces that would need the design decision.
